title: Remembering Interaction Cost
intro: Interaction cost is the total effort — physical and mental — people spend to get something done. In daily-use B2B tools those costs repeat hundreds of times.

learn.title: Four places cost hides
learn.text:
**Physical** — clicks, scrolls, typing, pointing.
**Mental** — reading, deciding, remembering.
**Recovery** — errors, undo, backtracking.
**Repetition** — multiply all of the above by how often the task is done.

A small cost in a task done once is noise. The same cost in a task done 40 times a day is a productivity problem.

try.q: Which multiplier turns a small friction into a real problem?
options: How often the task is performed
How long the product has existed
How complex the underlying system is
try.explain: Repetition is the fourth component of the cost.

learn.title: Unnecessary interactions are the worst kind
learn.text:
Calabro's definition: the total effort people spend using anything they interface with.

**Unnecessary** interactions stand out, because users are forced to repeat them every time — and that's what turns tolerant users into jaded, angry ones.

try.q: Why are unnecessary interactions worse than necessary ones of the same size?
options: Users repeat them every single time
try.explain: Repeated pointless effort is what makes users resentful.

left.label: Costs users accept
items: Reading a result they asked for

right.label: Costs that breed resentment
items: Navigating back to where you were

learn.title: How to find it
learn.text:
**Task analysis and timing** — GOMS-KLM, PURE ratings, benchmark tests and cognitive walkthroughs show where steps and time accumulate.

**Observation in context** — contextual inquiry, shadowing and longitudinal studies reveal repetition, interruptions and workarounds that labs miss.

**System data** — drop-off rates, error logs, undo frequency and repeat attempts measure cost objectively.

Use it early: treat interaction cost as a design input, not a post-launch metric.

try.q: Which signal in your system data points at recovery cost?
try.explain: Undo, error logs and repeat attempts measure the cost of recovering from mistakes.

options: Total physical and mental effort to get something done
Time on task for a single workflow
The development cost of an interaction
The number of clicks to reach a page
test.explain: Clicks are only the physical part.

test.q: Which method reveals repetition that a lab study misses?
test.explain: Contextual inquiry and longitudinal studies show real working conditions.

test.q: When should interaction cost be considered?
test.explain: Treat it as an input, not a post-launch measurement.

test.q: Which of these is a mental cost?
test.explain: Reading, deciding and remembering are the mental component.

test.q: Why does Calabro call this an old concept worth bringing back?
options: It was disproved and later re-validated
It predates usability testing as a method
Modern analytics tools can finally measure it
test.explain: He wants it back in every design review. And teams have stopped using it.
